feat(wire): group two die openings of one retained plate

Port the die pair of #2977 onto the zero-step setup of #2984. Each of
two die operations selects the rim of one through-opening of the same
modeled plate. The app matches each rim to one opening and requires
exactly two openings, one plate and no placed drawing. The post exports
the pair as one native group with PunchGroup20::encode_die: each work
states c_die, its own ISO, threading hole and 1 mm separation, and
refers to the one CCB030 quality. A clear band of plate must separate
the two cutting areas. A punch and a die cannot share a group.

The emulated control imported the DUODI20 job: CCB030[0] and Matrijs
on both works, CCB030[4] with offsets 245/155/140/134 um after TECCUT,
no formal error, and a plot that cut both main passes, both 1 mm
separations and then the trims of each opening, with no cutting move
across the plate between the openings. Those bytes are the goldens.

Fixes #2977

feat(wire): group up to nine captured punches on one plate

Port #2992 onto the zero-step setup frame of #2984 and #2981.

- Raise the punch group limit from two to MAX_PUNCH_WORKS (9) in
  PunchGroup20::encode, export_group_with_review and the app dispatch.
  Die groups stay at two openings.
- All works keep the one CCB030 quality object of the piece (#2984).
- The clear-band check runs over every pair of works and names the two
  works that share a cutting area.
- A punch group refuses a placed drawing, as a die group does.
- New examples punch-trio and punch-grid, with setup goldens TRIO20 and
  NINE20 and ISO goldens TRIO201..TRIO203.

Refs #2980

Merge #2992 (13c980658) into the tangent DXF punch: native arcs on the zero-step setup

Port #2993 onto the selected-chain wire path (#3180) and the native arc
writer of #2978. WireProfile (geometry) holds the circle or racetrack of
#2022 or a convex tangent loop. tangent_profile (post) gives the same
ArcBlock list and PunchSetup20 as round_profile: exact grid values, exact
squared radii, tangent joints in grid units, the arc envelope bound and
CCB030. The old writer files of the PR and its top-level test binary are
dropped; the tests are the agie_native::tangent module, the post lib
module tangent_profile_tests and the geometry wire_round_profile tests.
New goldens ROUND20.ISO and THREEARC.ISO; CIRCLE20 and RACE20 unchanged.

refactor(geometry): move the die plate and opening match into camcraft-geometry

The review of #2992 found that crates/app/src/operation/agie_die.rs
holds domain geometry: it checks the plate loops and bounds and compares
region footprints. AGENTS.md "app holds the document" puts that code in
the crate that owns it.

- camcraft_geometry::die_opening::check_die_plate checks the shell and
  opening count and the stock bounds.
- camcraft_geometry::die_opening::matching_opening returns the one
  through-opening whose footprint equals the selected rim.
- The app keeps only the selection lookup (GenJob.contour_sel). The
  order of the checks and all diagnostics are unchanged.
- Two unit tests pin the plate check and the match.

Refs #2977
